newsitem.title: USA: Lyondell-Citgo refinery upgrade near completion.
newsitem.headline: Lyondell-Citgo refinery upgrade near completion.

text.p: Lyondell-Citgo Refining Co is preparing to start a crude distillation unit and delayed coker installed at its Houston refinery as part of an upgrade to handle heavy Venezuelan crude oil, a Lyondell Petrochemical Co spokesman said Monday.

The rated capacity of the refinery will remain at 265,000 barrels per day (bpd) but the upgrades will allow the refinery to process 200,000 bpd of the heavy Venezuelan crude, up from 130,000 bpd, a Lyondell spokesman said.
"That will be essentially all the crude throughput of the refinery," spokesman David Harpole said. "They will have gotten out of the sweeter, lighter feedstocks."

The units will be started sometime in the first quarter, the company said in announcing its fourth quarter results. The upgrade also included installation of a hydrodesulphurization unit and a sulphur plant, which are already in service, Harpole said.
The upgrade is part of a Venezuelan crude oil supply agreement that will give Citgo, the domestic unit of Petroleos de Venezuela SA, a 40 percent stake in the refiney, Lyondell said.
